title: Hosted API escalation: runtime stability patch, retry-safety and customer mitigation
creator: Marco Liu
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported sustained 5xx spikes and long-tail timeouts on the Hosted API during tenant surges. Symptoms include increased p99 latency, socket pool exhaustion on frontdoor proxies, amplified retries from client SDKs, and KV cache compaction thrashing that correlated with a recent kernel selection change in runtime-1.20. Goal: stabilize hosted runtime, stop retry amplification, provide customer-facing mitigations, and ship a targeted runtime patch with telemetry. Scope: affects hosted endpoints only (customers on Dedicated/Private see partial degradation if routing to hosted fallbacks occurs). Hypothesis: an interaction between the new kernel scheduling heuristic and KV cache compaction under high tenant concurrency caused long-lived inference tasks to hold connections; those connections triggered client-side retries which amplified load and drove more KV compaction cycles, producing a feedback loop. Immediate impact: some tenants saw 5xx rates >2% for sustained windows and elevated error escalations from top-10 customers. Actions planned: 1) emergency mitigation: enable tenant-scoped admission control (soft-quarantine) and reduce max_inflight per tenant from 512 to 128 (feature flag roll) 2) SDK guidance: publish advisory to disable aggressive retries (exponential factor >2.5) and recommend idempotency tokens for critical requests 3) Hotfix: revert kernel heuristic change and add a guard in KV compaction to avoid compaction during high inflight windows (PR referenced below) 4) Observability: add tenant-level inflight gauge, socket pool exhaustion alerts, and a short-lived runbook dashboard 5) Canary + rollout: canary patch to 5% of capacity for 2h, monitor p99 and 5xx, then progressive rollout with rollback gate. Post-incident work: add automated tenant throttle policy, improve SDK retry defaults, and add an e2e test that simulates tenant-burst patterns.
